title: A Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Crossover Clinical Study of the Effects of Alpha-s1 Casein Hydrolysate on Sleep Disturbance

what_it_measured.text: This study evaluated the effects of alpha-s1 casein hydrolysate (ACH; Lactium® ) on the subjective and objective sleep profiles of a community-based sample of Koreans with poor sleep quality.

dose.text: The test capsule was composed of 75% ACH (300 mg), 24% maltodextrin, and 1% silicon dioxide. ACH was composed of 2.2% (6.6 mg) αS1 -casein (f91-100), which was detected by using high-performance liquid chromatography and photometric diode array.

route.text: Participants were asked to take either the test or placebo capsule every day an hour before their bedtime.

endpoint.text: Abstract: This study evaluated the effects of alpha-s1 casein hydrolysate (ACH; Lactium® ) on the subjective and objective sleep profiles of a community-based sample of Koreans with poor sleep quality.
We also assessed participants’ fatigue symptoms through the Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) [40].
In order to evaluate the safety of ACH, we assessed hematological profiles in addition to vital signs before and after each control and test phase (Supplementary Table S3).

reported_results.text: During the placebo phase, PSQI also decreased from baseline to the end of the phase, thus change in both groups was in the direction of improved sleep (p = 0.211). The sleep discomfort index (measured by ISI) was similar, with a significant effect of time (p < 0.001), although there was no statistically significant overall difference compared to the placebo phase (p = 0.523).

Participants’ daytime functioning also gradually improved during the four-week administration period; however, there were no significant differences between phases (ESS, p = 0.324; FSS, p = 0.854). Regarding depression and anxiety indicators, participants exhibited a similar tendency to improve during both ACH and placebo phases without significant group differences (BDI, p = 0.912; BAI, p = 0.924).
